\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مصروف} (masrūf)}{مصروف (masrūf)}]{\ur{مصروف} (masrūf) — busy}

\label{lesson:UR-C527-masruf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a break in work, then the Urdu for complete.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مصروف}}
\textbf{\ur{مصروف}} — \emph{masrūf} — \textquotedblleft{}busy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{مصروف} \ur{ہیں} \ur{تو} \ur{میں} \ur{کل} \ur{آؤں} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp masrūf haiṅ to maiṅ kal āūṅ gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you're busy, I'll come tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مصروف}} (\emph{masrūf}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{maṣrūf}, \textquotedblleft{}turned towards something, taken up with it\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masrūf}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masrūf}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āp masrūf haiṅ to maiṅ kal āūṅ gā.} — If you're busy, I'll come tomorrow.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a break in work, then the Urdu for complete, then say \emph{masrūf} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{مصروف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Busy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{فارغ} (fārigh)}{فارغ (fārigh)}]{\ur{فارغ} (fārigh) — free (not busy)}

Before the new one: say the Urdu for complete, then the Urdu for busy.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دستیاب} (dastyāb)}{دستیاب (dastyāb)}]{\ur{دستیاب} (dastyāb) — available}

\label{lesson:UR-C527-dastyab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for busy, then the Urdu for not busy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دستیاب}}
\textbf{\ur{دستیاب}} — \emph{dastyāb} — \textquotedblleft{}available\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{ٹکٹ} \ur{دستیاب} \ur{ہوئے} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{کل} \ur{جائیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar ṭikaṭ dastyāb hue to ham kal jāeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If tickets are available, we will go tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دستیاب}} (\emph{dastyāb}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{dastyāb}, \textquotedblleft{}come to hand\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{dast}, \textquotedblleft{}a hand\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{yāb-}, \textquotedblleft{}to find\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بہانہ} (bahānā)}{بہانہ (bahānā)}]{\ur{بہانہ} (bahānā) — an excuse}

\label{lesson:UR-C527-bahana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for not busy, then the Urdu for available.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بہانہ}}
\textbf{\ur{بہانہ}} — \emph{bahānā} — \textquotedblleft{}an excuse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{وہ} \ur{نہیں} \ur{آیا} \ur{تو} \ur{کوئی} \ur{بہانہ} \ur{بنائے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar voh nahīṅ āyā to koī bahānā banāe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If he doesn't come, he will make up some excuse.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بہانہ}} (\emph{bahānā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bahāna}, \textquotedblleft{}a pretext, an excuse\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar voh nahīṅ āyā to koī bahānā banāe gā.} — If he doesn't come, he will make up some excuse.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for not busy, then the Urdu for available, then say \emph{bahānā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اوبنا} (ūbnā)}{اوبنا (ūbnā)}]{\ur{اوبنا} (ūbnā) — to get bored; to be fed up}

\label{lesson:UR-C527-ubna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for available, then the Urdu for an excuse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اوبنا}}
\textbf{\ur{اوبنا}} — \emph{ūbnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to get bored; to be fed up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{بارش} \ur{نہیں} \ur{رکی} \ur{تو} \ur{بچے} \ur{اوب} \ur{جائیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bārish nahīṅ rukī to bachche ūb jāeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the rain doesn't stop, the children will get bored.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{انتظار} \ur{سے} \ur{اوب} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh intizār se ūb gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اوبنا}} (\emph{ūbnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ūbnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be agitated, to be bewildered\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{udvijatē}, \textquotedblleft{}shudders, recoils\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2087); the everyday sense \textquotedblleft{}to be bored, to be fed up\textquotedblright{} is a later one that CDIAL does not record.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ūbnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ūbnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar bārish nahīṅ rukī to bachche ūb jāeṅ ge.} — If the rain doesn't stop, the children will get bored.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for available, then the Urdu for an excuse, then say \emph{ūbnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{اوبنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To get bored; to be fed up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
